A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SmallKV. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference-efficiency measurements, component ablations, attention-similarity analyses, and a generation case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on auxiliary-model cache compression, early stopping, and attention similarity across additional settings.

M1.justification: The core compensation mechanisms and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 introduces and evaluates an optional adaptation that stops the auxiliary model at earlier layers during attention mapping. Auxiliary-cache compression and speculative-decoding integration were already suggested in v1.

E1.justification: Table 7 adds MMLU to the attention-similarity evaluation. The existing GSM8K, BBH, MT-Bench, LongBench, and WikiText coverage is retained; the additional model pairings are configuration changes rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain H2O and PyramidInfer, while efficiency comparisons retain Accelerate with Eager/Flash attention and H2O. Appendix A.3 reuses H2O. Table 6 labels its reference column 'H3O', but the accompanying discussion identifies it as H2O.

E3.justification: New protocols fix the LLM cache at 20% while varying auxiliary-cache budgets and stopping layers, and introduce a comparison accounting for both models' caches. Appendix B adds model-pair configurations, including Qwen3, excludes initial attention-sink tokens in new similarity analyses, and measures similarity over five dialogue turns. Existing main benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds sensitivity analyses testing how auxiliary-cache compression and layer truncation affect accuracy. Appendix B substantially broadens checks of the attention-similarity premise across model families, benchmarks, and dialogue turns. The original component ablation, model-size study, heatmap, and generation case study remain.

E5.justification: The new tables report point estimates without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing uncertainty presentation, including Figure 1's error bars, is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 4–9 and the new Figure 9 add substantial overhead, sensitivity, and similarity results. For example, Table 5 reports BBH accuracy of 0.4416 and 0.4624 at 40% and 60% auxiliary-cache budgets, respectively; Table 9 reports similarity declining from 0.822 to 0.782 across five turns. Original benchmark and efficiency results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), the formal method definitions, and Appendix C's perturbation/error derivation are unchanged. The added numerical resource estimates do not introduce a new formal argument or revise the existing assumptions and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about the two compensation mechanisms, performance under restricted cache budgets, Flash Attention compatibility, and 1.75–2.56 times throughput improvement.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning weaker cross-family attention similarity, attention sinks inflating similarity measurements, and the trade-off between auxiliary-cache compression and saliency-shift compensation. It also discusses early stopping when draft-token generation is unnecessary. The existing limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds deployment guidance specifying auxiliary-layer stopping points, cache-budget combinations, and combined memory accounting, including the estimated 7.14% auxiliary-cache footprint. Hardware, software versions, matching-length guidance, implementation pseudocode, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused paragraph on speculative decoding, including its reported speedups and commercial adoption. It uses references already present in v1; the bibliography and principal novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. Local additions include Appendix A.3, expanded Appendix B discussion, and the speculative-decoding paragraph. Author affiliations, contribution/contact footnotes, funding acknowledgments, and the conference designation are updated.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation expands substantially through Tables 4–9 and a new attention-comparison Figure 9. Figure 2 changes from stacked to side-by-side panels, and Figures 6–7 are enlarged and relocated. The retained generation example becomes Figure 10 on a separate page; it is not a new case study.

improvement.justification: The added auxiliary-model sensitivity tests and broader attention-similarity checks provide useful support for practical deployment and applicability. The gain is limited by reporting weaknesses: Appendix A.3 claims 0.462 accuracy at a 40% auxiliary-cache budget, whereas Table 5 reports 0.4416 there and 0.4624 at 60%; the new multi-turn analysis also lacks clear dataset and model specifications. The core method and principal results remain unchanged.
